issues.what: Mrs Pruett re-delivers the chapter 1 hem deduction as if new, with different facts (park mud, walked not cabbed, taught Theodore), and Honora says she was never told.
issues.quote: I read your hem the day you came to my door, before you had your coat off

issues.what: Timeline: says Miss Vane came Monday; she came the morning of the case (Wednesday). Ch1 says she had until 'this morning', ch3-5 say dismissed Tuesday.
issues.quote: Miss Vane came to them Monday while they were in Devon.

issues.what: Letters were left behind the false back in ch3/4 but appear from a kitchen chest of drawers under a pudding cloth.
issues.quote: where Mrs Pruett had laid them under a pudding cloth

issues.what: Letter addressed to 'Miss E. Nott' contradicts the young man Edward writing them; 'Edgeware' misspelt.
issues.quote: Miss E. Nott, care of the Bell, Edgeware.

issues.what: Lady Cantle was at home in ch2 yet is fetched 'home' from her sister's with no explanation; Dr Marsh called 'Mr Marsh'; Charlotte (8) called a seven year old.
issues.quote: a seven year old for help

issues.what: Buttons: one was dropped by Charlotte (called 'nursery issue'), not both found in the chest; 'your brother' should be brother-in-law; Theodore credited with Charlotte's clue; 'this morning' for an afternoon forgery; 'a day before you'.
issues.quote: Two brass buttons in the chest with the locket.

issues.what: Opens by repeating ch4's closing line verbatim.
issues.quote: Mrs Pruett did not nod. Not yet.

fix: Ch4: replace the repeated hem recap with a question about Monday night that seeds Edward; fix letter signature, Richmond errand, Dr Marsh, age. Ch1: dismissal the night before. Ch5: 'this morning', letters fetched by Kit, buttons, brother-in-law, Charlotte's clue, Pruett, afternoon, drop repeated opener. Retitle ch3.
praise: Mrs Pruett is a delight - tart, competent, never thanked - and the almost-thank-you breakfast lands perfectly.

issues.what: The overheard bargain changes: ch1 is noon, with Gopinath, two noblemen and the factor, 'yesterday'; ch3-5 make it dusk 'last week', alone, jemadars with Watts, Clive and gold mohurs.
issues.quote: At the warehouse last week, you brought yarn at dusk.

issues.what: Shirin retells the overheard scene to Gopinath 'not told whole' though he was beside her, and ch5 repeats the same speech near-verbatim to Nasrin.
issues.quote: Last week at the warehouse, I have not told it whole.

issues.what: Bribe sum drifts from forty thousand rupees (ch1) to forty lakhs (ch4, ch5).
issues.quote: Watts said, forty lakhs upon signature

issues.what: Duplicate chapter title: ch1 and ch2 are both 'The Pattern Book'.
History: Plassey was fought in June as a heavy rain spoiled the Nawab's uncovered powder, not before the rains with guns stuck in mud; Clive's army came from downriver, not upriver (ch4).
issues.quote: when the rains were still holding off

issues.what: Hale asks what the turned diamond means as if for the first time and gets a different answer than in ch3; Gopinath says he taught Shirin 'when she was small'.
issues.quote: What does this mean? he asked.

issues.what: Repeated images: 'light as breath' / 'held breath', knuckles 'swollen to the size of tamarind seeds' verbatim twice, brass pot ringing against stone twice, river knocking at pilings.
issues.quote: The joints were swollen to the size of tamarind seeds.

fix: Ch3-5: make every reference to the overheard bargain match ch1 (noon, veranda, two noblemen, factor, forty thousand); cut the ch4 retelling to what Gopinath missed and shorten ch5's speech; correct Plassey rain and downriver; Hale's second question acknowledges the first; retitle ch2; trim repeated phrases.
praise: Exact, tactile craft detail and an honestly bitter ending - the warning arrives and history does not bend.
